thread:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - elevated errors for tenant 'zenith-enterprise' in dedicated pool dp-eu-west-2. Detection: sustained token gen failures + KV miss spike.

Aarav (oncall-sre): Picking this up. Initial glance: large drop in tenant KV prefix cache hit-rate, spike in prefix creation events. Latency climbing.

infra-bot: Pool dp-eu-west-2 GPU usage 64%. No node OOMs. Routing fallback triggered for ~18% of requests in last 10m.

Marta (prod-eng): Runtime logs showing heavy churn on tenant prefixes. Example: ```
[2026-04-02T09:12:03Z] tenant=zenith-enterprise prefix=zenith:tmp:* cache_miss key='zenith:tmp:20260402:abcd'
[2026-04-02T09:12:10Z] tenant=zenith-enterprise prefix=zenith:session:* cache_miss key='zenith:session:tmp:xyz'
redis_stats: keys=12.3M evicted=1.02M used=22GB
```

Lee (eng-runtime): Likely root cause: customer-side job writing high-cardinality ephemeral keys (bad key schema). That floods prefix cache and collapses hit-rate. Two live mitigations: A) disable prefix caching for tenant (fast config flip, stops pollution but increases per-KV latency), B) targeted eviction of ephemeral prefixes plus temporary write-rate limiting. Need customer consent for anything affecting latency.

Julia G (CSE): On the customer call now. They report interactive UI slowdowns and intermittent timeouts. They're on a dedicated/reserved pool; they prefer no restarts. They can accept a brief maintenance window and prefer eviction first.

Aarav (oncall-sre): I'll prepare eviction and rate-limit. Proposed sequence: 1) apply conservative write-rate cap 2) dry-run scan for patterns `zenith:tmp:*` and `zenith:session_tmp:*` 3) targeted delete 4) monitor. If doesn't improve, flip off prefix cache for tenant.

Sam T (next-oncall): I'll take the handoff later. Keep me posted before any config flips.

Marta (prod-eng): Dry-run scan results: `SCAN` returned ~9.6M matches for `zenith:tmp:*`. Hot fragments: `zenith:tmp:20260402` -> ~3.8M keys. That's definitely the culprit.

Aarav (oncall-sre): Applying temporary write cap 60 rps for the tenant now.

infra-bot: Action log: write cap set for tenant zenith-enterprise by Aarav at 09:18 UTC.

Marta (prod-eng): Preparing deletion script. Will run with customer heads-up. Script uses `--scan` then batch delete to avoid blocking. Example: `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'zenith:tmp:*' | xargs -r -n1000 redis-cli DEL`. We'll test a small batch first.

Julia G (CSE): Customer OKs targeted deletion. They want a 5-minute heads-up before we start.

Aarav (oncall-sre): Starting small-batch delete in 5m. Monitoring dashboards and logs. Rollback plan: re-enable prefix cache or revert deletes? (can't revert deletes) Primary rollback is to enable model routing fallback to avoid timeouts.

Marta (prod-eng): Executed batch delete (first 50k keys). Observed immediate uptick in KV prefix hit-rate: 7% -> 34% within 45s. Tail latency dropped from ~6.8s -> ~2.1s. Error rate decreasing.

Lee (eng-runtime): Given improvement, hold on config flip. I'll stage the prefix cache disable command but won't execute: `POST /internal/config/tenants/zenith-enterprise/cache {"prefix_cache_enabled":false}`.

Aarav (oncall-sre): I'll keep write cap for another 30m to prevent re-pollution. Noting that deleting ephemeral keys is destructive; customer asked for confirmation and accepted.

Sam T (next-oncall): I'll watch metrics during handoff at 10:00 UTC. If things re-regress, I'll perform the pre-approved cache-disabling change.

Julia G (CSE): Customer thanks the team and requested a short postmortem. They believe a nightly data-export job was misconfigured and creating tmp keys. They're going to patch on their side.

Marta (prod-eng): Filing follow-up ticket: add runtime guard to detect tenant key-cardinality spikes and auto-alert CSE/ops, plus consider auto-quarantine of new high-card-prefixes.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Customer-facing update scheduled by Julia.

Aarav (oncall-sre): Final notes for handoff: eviction completed in batches, write-cap 60rps in place, monitoring alerts tightened for 24h, prepared config flip ready. Handing to Sam. Good job.

Sam T (next-oncall): Acknowledged. Will keep throttling for 30m then coordinate with CSE to remove if stable. I will open postmortem doc and assign follow-ups.
